name: Global Climate Coalition

summary.text: The Global Climate Coalition (GCC) was an industry group formed in 1989 under the National Association of Manufacturers to represent fossil fuel, automotive and manufacturing interests in climate policy debates. Founding members named in reporting include the American Petroleum Institute, Shell Oil, Exxon and General Motors; Exxon was a founding member of its board. A December 1995 draft science primer written for the coalition by Mobil's Lenny Bernstein stated that the scientific basis for the greenhouse effect 'is well established and cannot be denied', while a public backgrounder the coalition gave lawmakers said the role of greenhouse gases 'is not well understood'. The GCC spent more than $13 million on advertising against the Kyoto Protocol in 1997, lost members after BP left in May 1997, and disbanded in early 2002.

facts.claim: The Global Climate Coalition was formed in 1989 under the umbrella of the National Association of Manufacturers. Reporting names the American Petroleum Institute, Shell Oil, Exxon and General Motors among its founding members, alongside more than 40 other corporations.
facts.quote: A Down to Earth article names the American Petroleum Institute, Shell Oil, Exxon, and General Motors among its founding members, plus more than 40 other corporations.

facts.claim: A draft primer titled 'Predicting Future Climate Change: A Primer', dated December 1995 and written for the GCC by Lenny Bernstein of Mobil Corporation, stated that the scientific basis for the greenhouse effect and the potential impact of human emissions on climate was well established and could not be denied. A January 1996 draft prepared for the coalition's Science and Technical Advisory Committee repeated that wording.
facts.quote: The draft primer said the scientific basis for the greenhouse effect and the potential impact of human emissions on climate is well established and cannot be denied.

facts.claim: Bernstein's draft primer described the contrarian theories of Richard Lindzen and Patrick Michaels as not convincing. According to the coalition's minutes as reported by DeSmog, its advisory committee approved the primer only after agreeing to omit that section; the final version excluded the comments, the primer was never distributed publicly, and the GCC continued to cite the two scientists.
facts.quote: Bernstein's draft called the work of Richard Lindzen and Patrick Michaels "not convincing," but the final copy of that document excluded any mention of these comments and the GCC continued to cite the two.

sources.title: The 'Historical Jigsaw of Climate Deception': Private Notes Show How Big Oil Spread Climate Science Denial

facts.claim: Through the early 1990s the coalition distributed a scientific 'backgrounder' to lawmakers and journalists stating that the role of greenhouse gases in climate change 'is not well understood'.
facts.quote: The coalition said in a scientific "backgrounder" provided to lawmakers and journalists through the early 1990s that the role of greenhouse gases in climate change "is not well understood."

sources.title: Tweet the Story of the Fossil Fuel Industry's Climate Deception

facts.claim: In 1997 the GCC spent more than $13 million on an advertising campaign against the Kyoto Protocol, according to DeSmog citing the Los Angeles Times. The ads, which ran in the New York Times among other outlets, were placed through the Global Climate Information Project, co-sponsored by the GCC and the American Automobile Manufacturers Association, and argued the treaty was unfair because developing nations faced no reduction requirements.
facts.quote: DeSmog, citing the Los Angeles Times, reports that the GCC spent over $13 million on its 1997 ad campaign against the Kyoto Protocol.

facts.claim: The GCC's membership shrank after BP left the coalition in May 1997. The coalition disbanded in early 2002, stating that it had served its purpose by contributing to a new national approach to global warming.
facts.quote: The GCC disbanded in early 2002, explaining that it "has served its purpose by contributing to a new national approach to global warming."

connections.claim: The Global Climate Coalition was formed in 1989 as a project operating under the umbrella of the National Association of Manufacturers.
connections.quote: The GCC was formed in 1989 under the National Association of Manufacturers. One source describes it as a project run under that group's umbrella.

connections.claim: Exxon, later ExxonMobil, was a founding member of the Global Climate Coalition and a founding member of its board of directors.
connections.quote: Exxon, later ExxonMobil, was a founding member, and a founding member of the GCC's board of directors.

openQuestions: Membership claims rest on DeSmog and Down to Earth; the GCC's own membership lists in the Climate Files collection should be checked.
Powerbase gives 2001 rather than 2002 for the coalition's dissolution.
The $13 million advertising figure is DeSmog's citation of the Los Angeles Times; the original article was not opened.
The 1995 primer story was first reported by the New York Times in 2009; that article could not be reached.
